Add a new "rate-limit" middleware to this Hono framework codebase.

Requirements:
- Create src/middleware/rate-limit/index.ts with the middleware implementation
- Follow the exact same patterns as other middleware (compress, cache, bearer-auth):
  - Export a factory function that returns MiddlewareHandler
  - Use an options interface (RateLimitOptions) with sensible defaults
  - Import types from "../../types"
- Options should include:
  - limit: number (default 100) — max requests per window
  - windowMs: number (default 60000) — time window in ms
  - keyGenerator?: (c: Context) => string — defaults to remote IP
  - skip?: (c: Context) => boolean — skip rate limiting for certain requests
  - handler?: (c: Context) => Response | Promise<Response> — custom 429 response
- Return 429 Too Many Requests when limit exceeded with JSON body
- Add the middleware to src/middleware/rate-limit/index.test.ts following the same
  test patterns as other middleware tests (use Hono app setup, supertest-style requests)

Commit your changes.


IMPORTANT: Always git add and git commit your changes before finishing.

- oobo: Context beyond the diff - captures AI sessions, tokens, code attribution, semantic code search, and engineering memory via MCP. Use when the user asks about commit history with AI context, session history, code attribution, token usage, code search, or engineering memory.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the current diff and apply the fixes — equivalent to /code-review --fix.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	/**
2	 * @module
3	 * Bearer Auth Middleware for Hono.
4	 */
5	
6	import type { Context } from '../../context'
7	import { HTTPException } from '../../http-exception'
8	import type { Env, MiddlewareHandler } from '../../types'
9	import { timingSafeEqual } from '../../utils/buffer'
10	import type { ContentfulStatusCode } from '../../utils/http-status'
11	
12	const TOKEN_STRINGS = '[A-Za-z0-9._~+/-]+=*'
13	const PREFIX = 'Bearer'
14	const HEADER = 'Authorization'
15	
16	type MessageFunction = (c: Context) => string | object | Promise<string | object>
17	type CustomizedErrorResponseOptions = {
18	  wwwAuthenticateHeader?: string | object | MessageFunction
19	  message?: string | object | MessageFunction
20	}
21	
22	type BearerAuthOptions<E extends Env = Env> =
23	  | {
24	      token: string | string[]
25	      realm?: string
26	      prefix?: string
27	      headerName?: string
28	      hashFunction?: Function
29	      /**
30	       * @deprecated Use noAuthenticationHeader.message instead
31	       */
32	      noAuthenticationHeaderMessage?: string | object | MessageFunction
33	      noAuthenticationHeader?: CustomizedErrorResponseOptions
34	      /**
35	       * @deprecated Use invalidAuthenticationHeader.message instead
36	       */
37	      invalidAuthenticationHeaderMessage?: string | object | MessageFunction
38	      invalidAuthenticationHeader?: CustomizedErrorResponseOptions
39	      /**
40	       * @deprecated Use invalidToken.message instead
41	       */
42	      invalidTokenMessage?: string | object | MessageFunction
43	      invalidToken?: CustomizedErrorResponseOptions
44	    }
45	  | {
46	      realm?: string
47	      prefix?: string
48	      headerName?: string
49	      verifyToken: (token: string, c: Context<E>) => boolean | Promise<boolean>
50	      hashFunction?: Function
51	      /**
52	       * @deprecated Use noAuthenticationHeader.message instead
53	       */
54	      noAuthenticationHeaderMessage?: string | object | MessageFunction
55	      noAuthenticationHeader?: CustomizedErrorResponseOptions
56	      /**
57	       * @deprecated Use invalidAuthenticationHeader.message instead
58	       */
59	      invalidAuthenticationHeaderMessage?: string | object | MessageFunction
60	      invalidAuthenticationHeader?: CustomizedErrorResponseOptions
61	      /**
62	       * @deprecated Use invalidToken.message instead
63	       */
64	      invalidTokenMessage?: string | object | MessageFunction
65	      invalidToken?: CustomizedErrorResponseOptions
66	    }
67	
68	/**
69	 * Bearer Auth Middleware for Hono.
70	 *
71	 * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/bearer-auth}
72	 *
73	 * @template E - The environment type.
74	 * @param {BearerAuthOptions} options - The options for the bearer authentication middleware.
75	 * @param {string | string[]} [options.token] - The string or array of strings to validate the incoming bearer token against.
76	 * @param {Function} [options.verifyToken] - The function to verify the token.
77	 * @param {string} [options.realm=""] - The domain name of the realm, as part of the returned WWW-Authenticate challenge header.
78	 * @param {string} [options.prefix="Bearer"] - The prefix (or known as `schema`) for the Authorization header value. If set to the empty string, no prefix is expected.
79	 * @param {string} [options.headerName=Authorization] - The header name.
80	 * @param {Function} [options.hashFunction] - A function to handle hashing for safe comparison of authentication tokens.
81	 * @param {string | object | MessageFunction} [options.noAuthenticationHeader.message="Unauthorized"] - The no authentication header message.
82	 * @param {string | object | MessageFunction} [options.noAuthenticationHeader.wwwAuthenticateHeader="Bearer realm=\"\""] - The response header value for the WWW-Authenticate header when no authentication header is provided.
83	 * @param {string | object | MessageFunction} [options.invalidAuthenticationHeader.message="Bad Request"] - The invalid authentication header message.
84	 * @param {string | object | MessageFunction} [options.invalidAuthenticationHeader.wwwAuthenticateHeader="Bearer error=\"invalid_request\""] - The response header value for the WWW-Authenticate header when authentication header is invalid.
85	 * @param {string | object | MessageFunction} [options.invalidToken.message="Unauthorized"] - The invalid token message.
86	 * @param {string | object | MessageFunction} [options.invalidToken.wwwAuthenticateHeader="Bearer error=\"invalid_token\""] - The response header value for the WWW-Authenticate header when token is invalid.
87	 * @returns {MiddlewareHandler<E>} The middleware handler function.
88	 * @throws {Error} If neither "token" nor "verifyToken" options are provided.
89	 * @throws {HTTPException} If authentication fails, with 401 status code for missing or invalid token, or 400 status code for invalid request.
90	 *
91	 * @example
92	 * ```ts
93	 * const app = new Hono()
94	 *
95	 * const token = 'honoishot'
96	 *
97	 * app.use('/api/*', bearerAuth({ token }))
98	 *
99	 * app.get('/api/page', (c) => {
100	 *   return c.json({ message: 'You are authorized' })
101	 * })
102	 * ```
103	 */
104	export const bearerAuth = <E extends Env = Env>(
105	  options: BearerAuthOptions<E>
106	): MiddlewareHandler<E> => {
107	  if (!('token' in options || 'verifyToken' in options)) {
108	    throw new Error('bearer auth middleware requires options for "token"')
109	  }
110	  if (!options.realm) {
111	    options.realm = ''
112	  }
113	  if (options.prefix === undefined) {
114	    options.prefix = PREFIX
115	  }
116	
117	  const realm = options.realm?.replace(/"/g, '\\"')
118	  const prefix = options.prefix
119	  const tokenRegexp = new RegExp(`^${TOKEN_STRINGS}$`)
120	  const wwwAuthenticatePrefix = prefix === '' ? '' : `${prefix} `
121	
122	  const throwHTTPException = async (
123	    c: Context,
124	    status: ContentfulStatusCode,
125	    wwwAuthenticateHeader: string | object | MessageFunction,
126	    messageOption: string | object | MessageFunction
127	  ): Promise<Response> => {
128	    const wwwAuthenticateHeaderValue: string | object =
129	      typeof wwwAuthenticateHeader === 'function'
130	        ? await wwwAuthenticateHeader(c)
131	        : wwwAuthenticateHeader
132	
133	    const headers = {
134	      'WWW-Authenticate':
135	        typeof wwwAuthenticateHeaderValue === 'string'
136	          ? wwwAuthenticateHeaderValue
137	          : `${wwwAuthenticatePrefix}${Object.entries(wwwAuthenticateHeaderValue)
138	              .map(([key, value]) => `${key}="${value}"`)
139	              .join(',')}`,
140	    }
141	    const responseMessage =
142	      typeof messageOption === 'function' ? await messageOption(c) : messageOption
143	    const res =
144	      typeof responseMessage === 'string'
145	        ? new Response(responseMessage, { status, headers })
146	        : new Response(JSON.stringify(responseMessage), {
147	            status,
148	            headers: {
149	              ...headers,
150	              'content-type': 'application/json',
151	            },
152	          })
153	    throw new HTTPException(status, { res })
154	  }
155	
156	  return async function bearerAuth(c, next) {
157	    const headerToken = c.req.header(options.headerName || HEADER)
158	    if (!headerToken) {
159	      // No Authorization header
160	      await throwHTTPException(
161	        c,
162	        401,
163	        options.noAuthenticationHeader?.wwwAuthenticateHeader ||
164	          `${wwwAuthenticatePrefix}realm="${realm}"`,
165	        options.noAuthenticationHeader?.message ||
166	          options.noAuthenticationHeaderMessage ||
167	          'Unauthorized'
168	      )
169	    } else {
170	      let tokenValue: string | undefined
171	
172	      if (prefix === '') {
173	        tokenValue = headerToken
174	      } else {
175	        const headerLower = headerToken.toLowerCase()
176	        const prefixLower = prefix.toLowerCase()
177	        if (headerLower.startsWith(prefixLower) && headerToken[prefix.length] === ' ') {
178	          tokenValue = headerToken.slice(prefix.length).trimStart()
179	        }
180	      }
181	
182	      if (!tokenValue || !tokenRegexp.test(tokenValue)) {
183	        // Invalid Request
184	        await throwHTTPException(
185	          c,
186	          400,
187	          options.invalidAuthenticationHeader?.wwwAuthenticateHeader ||
188	            `${wwwAuthenticatePrefix}error="invalid_request"`,
189	          options.invalidAuthenticationHeader?.message ||
190	            options.invalidAuthenticationHeaderMessage ||
191	            'Bad Request'
192	        )
193	      } else {
194	        let equal = false
195	        if ('verifyToken' in options) {
196	          equal = await options.verifyToken(tokenValue, c)
197	        } else if (typeof options.token === 'string') {
198	          equal = await timingSafeEqual(options.token, tokenValue, options.hashFunction)
199	        } else if (Array.isArray(options.token) && options.token.length > 0) {
200	          for (const token of options.token) {
201	            if (await timingSafeEqual(token, tokenValue, options.hashFunction)) {
202	              equal = true
203	              break
204	            }
205	          }
206	        }
207	        if (!equal) {
208	          // Invalid Token
209	          await throwHTTPException(
210	            c,
211	            401,
212	            options.invalidToken?.wwwAuthenticateHeader ||
213	              `${wwwAuthenticatePrefix}error="invalid_token"`,
214	            options.invalidToken?.message || options.invalidTokenMessage || 'Unauthorized'
215	          )
216	        }
217	      }
218	    }
219	    await next()
220	  }
221	}

1	/**
2	 * @module
3	 * Compress Middleware for Hono.
4	 */
5	
6	import type { MiddlewareHandler } from '../../types'
7	import { parseAccept } from '../../utils/accept'
8	import { COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX } from '../../utils/compress'
9	
10	export { COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX }
11	
12	const ENCODING_TYPES = ['gzip', 'deflate'] as const
13	type Encoding = (typeof ENCODING_TYPES)[number]
14	const cacheControlNoTransformRegExp = /(?:^|,)\s*?no-transform\s*?(?:,|$)/i
15	
16	type ContentTypeFilter = RegExp | ((contentType: string) => boolean)
17	
18	interface CompressionOptions {
19	  encoding?: Encoding
20	  threshold?: number
21	  contentTypeFilter?: ContentTypeFilter
22	}
23	
24	const selectEncoding = (
25	  header: string | undefined,
26	  candidates: readonly Encoding[]
27	): Encoding | undefined => {
28	  if (header === undefined) {
29	    return undefined
30	  }
31	  const accepts = parseAccept(header)
32	  const wildcardQ = accepts.find((a) => a.type === '*')?.q
33	  let best: { encoding: Encoding; q: number } | undefined
34	  for (const enc of candidates) {
35	    const explicit = accepts.find((a) => a.type.toLowerCase() === enc)
36	    const q = explicit ? explicit.q : (wildcardQ ?? 0)
37	    if (q === 1) {
38	      return enc
39	    } else if (q > 0 && (!best || q > best.q)) {
40	      best = { encoding: enc, q }
41	    }
42	  }
43	  return best?.encoding
44	}
45	
46	/**
47	 * Compress Middleware for Hono.
48	 *
49	 * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/compress}
50	 *
51	 * @param {CompressionOptions} [options] - The options for the compress middleware.
52	 * @param {'gzip' | 'deflate'} [options.encoding] - The compression scheme to allow for response compression. Either 'gzip' or 'deflate'. If not defined, both are allowed and will be used based on the Accept-Encoding header. 'gzip' is prioritized if this option is not provided and the client provides both in the Accept-Encoding header.
53	 * @param {number} [options.threshold=1024] - The minimum size in bytes to compress. Defaults to 1024 bytes.
54	 * @param {RegExp | Function} [options.contentTypeFilter=COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX] - A RegExp or function to determine if the response Content-Type should be compressed.
55	 * @returns {MiddlewareHandler} The middleware handler function.
56	 *
57	 * @example
58	 * ```ts
59	 * const app = new Hono()
60	 *
61	 * app.use(compress())
62	 *
63	 * // Compress only JSON responses
64	 * app.use(compress({ contentTypeFilter: /^application\/json/ }))
65	 *
66	 * // Compress based on custom Content-Type logic
67	 * app.use(compress({ contentTypeFilter: (type) => COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX.test(type) || type === "application/x-myformat" }))
68	 * ```
69	 */
70	export const compress = (options?: CompressionOptions): MiddlewareHandler => {
71	  const threshold = options?.threshold ?? 1024
72	  const candidates: readonly Encoding[] = options?.encoding ? [options.encoding] : ENCODING_TYPES
73	
74	  const contentTypeFilter = options?.contentTypeFilter ?? COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX
75	  const shouldCompress =
76	    typeof contentTypeFilter === 'function'
77	      ? (res: Response) => {
78	          const type = res.headers.get('Content-Type')
79	          return type && contentTypeFilter(type)
80	        }
81	      : (res: Response) => {
82	          const type = res.headers.get('Content-Type')
83	          return type && contentTypeFilter.test(type)
84	        }
85	
86	  return async function compress(ctx, next) {
87	    await next()
88	
89	    const contentLength = ctx.res.headers.get('Content-Length')
90	
91	    // Check if response should be compressed
92	    if (
93	      ctx.res.headers.has('Content-Encoding') || // already encoded
94	      ctx.res.headers.has('Transfer-Encoding') || // already encoded or chunked
95	      ctx.req.method === 'HEAD' || // HEAD request
96	      (contentLength && Number(contentLength) < threshold) || // content-length below threshold
97	      !shouldCompress(ctx.res) || // not compressible type
98	      !shouldTransform(ctx.res) // cache-control: no-transform
99	    ) {
100	      return
101	    }
102	
103	    const accepted = ctx.req.header('Accept-Encoding')
104	    const encoding = selectEncoding(accepted, candidates)
105	    if (!encoding || !ctx.res.body) {
106	      return
107	    }
108	
109	    // Compress the response
110	    const stream = new CompressionStream(encoding)
111	    ctx.res = new Response(ctx.res.body.pipeThrough(stream), ctx.res)
112	    ctx.res.headers.delete('Content-Length')
113	    ctx.res.headers.set('Content-Encoding', encoding)
114	
115	    // Convert strong ETag to weak ETag since compressed content is not byte-identical
116	    const etag = ctx.res.headers.get('ETag')
117	    if (etag && !etag.startsWith('W/')) {
118	      ctx.res.headers.set('ETag', `W/${etag}`)
119	    }
120	  }
121	}
122	
123	const shouldTransform = (res: Response) => {
124	  const cacheControl = res.headers.get('Cache-Control')
125	  // Don't compress for Cache-Control: no-transform
126	  // https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7234#section-5.2.2.4
127	  return !cacheControl || !cacheControlNoTransformRegExp.test(cacheControl)
128	}

2	 * @module
3	 * Body Limit Middleware for Hono.
4	 */
5	
6	import type { Context } from '../../context'
7	import { HTTPException } from '../../http-exception'
8	import type { MiddlewareHandler } from '../../types'
9	
10	const ERROR_MESSAGE = 'Payload Too Large'
11	
12	type OnError = (c: Context) => Response | Promise<Response>
13	type BodyLimitOptions = {
14	  maxSize: number
15	  onError?: OnError
16	}
17	
18	/**
19	 * Body Limit Middleware for Hono.
20	 *
21	 * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/middleware/builtin/body-limit}
22	 *
23	 * @param {BodyLimitOptions} options - The options for the body limit middleware.
24	 * @param {number} options.maxSize - The maximum body size allowed.
25	 * @param {OnError} [options.onError] - The error handler to be invoked if the specified body size is exceeded.
26	 * @returns {MiddlewareHandler} The middleware handler function.
27	 *
28	 * @example
29	 * ```ts
30	 * const app = new Hono()
31	 *
32	 * app.post(
33	 *   '/upload',
34	 *   bodyLimit({
35	 *     maxSize: 50 * 1024, // 50kb
36	 *     onError: (c) => {
37	 *       return c.text('overflow :(', 413)
38	 *     },
39	 *   }),
40	 *   async (c) => {
41	 *     const body = await c.req.parseBody()
42	 *     if (body['file'] instanceof File) {
43	 *       console.log(`Got file sized: ${body['file'].size}`)
44	 *     }
45	 *     return c.text('pass :)')
46	 *   }
47	 * )
48	 * ```
49	 */
50	export const bodyLimit = (options: BodyLimitOptions): MiddlewareHandler => {
51	  const onError: OnError =
52	    options.onError ||
53	    (() => {
54	      const res = new Response(ERROR_MESSAGE, {
55	        status: 413,
56	      })
57	      throw new HTTPException(413, { res })
58	    })
59	  const maxSize = options.maxSize
60	
61	  return async function bodyLimit(c, next) {
62	    if (!c.req.raw.body) {
63	      // maybe GET or HEAD request
64	      return next()
65	    }
66	
67	    const hasTransferEncoding = c.req.raw.headers.has('transfer-encoding')
68	    const hasContentLength = c.req.raw.headers.has('content-length')
69	
70	    if (hasContentLength && !hasTransferEncoding) {
71	      // Only Content-Length present - we can trust it
72	      const contentLength = parseInt(c.req.raw.headers.get('content-length') || '0', 10)
73	      return contentLength > maxSize ? onError(c) : next()
74	    }
75	
76	    // Transfer-Encoding present (chunked) or no length headers.
77	    // Per RFC 7230, when both are present Transfer-Encoding takes precedence
78	    // and Content-Length is ignored. Read the body up-front so the size check
79	    // is final before the handler runs, regardless of how (or whether) the
80	    // handler reads the body.
81	    let size = 0
82	    const chunks: Uint8Array[] = []
83	    const rawReader = c.req.raw.body.getReader()
84	    for (;;) {
85	      const { done, value } = await rawReader.read()
86	      if (done) {
87	        break
88	      }
89	      size += value.length
90	      if (size > maxSize) {
91	        return onError(c)
92	      }
93	      chunks.push(value)
94	    }
95	
96	    const requestInit: RequestInit & { duplex: 'half' } = {
97	      body: new ReadableStream({
98	        start(controller) {
99	          for (const chunk of chunks) {
100	            controller.enqueue(chunk)
101	          }
102	          controller.close()
103	        },
104	      }),
105	      duplex: 'half',
106	    }
107	    c.req.raw = new Request(c.req.raw, requestInit as RequestInit)
108	
109	    return next()
110	  }
111	}

33	 *   await someLongRunningFunction()
34	 *   return c.text('Completed within time limit')
35	 * })
36	 * ```
37	 */
38	export const timeout = (
39	  duration: number,
40	  exception: HTTPExceptionFunction | HTTPException = defaultTimeoutException
41	): MiddlewareHandler => {
42	  return async function timeout(context, next) {
43	    let timer: number | undefined
44	    const timeoutPromise = new Promise<void>((_, reject) => {
45	      timer = setTimeout(() => {
46	        reject(typeof exception === 'function' ? exception(context) : exception)
47	      }, duration) as unknown as number
48	    })
49	
50	    try {
51	      await Promise.race([next(), timeoutPromise])
52	    } finally {
53	      if (timer !== undefined) {
54	        clearTimeout(timer)
55	      }
56	    }
57	  }
58	}
